text:
Minnesota needed a three-goal burst in the second period to build a 5-2 lead, and then needed every bit of it. St. Louis scored twice in the final four minutes, the last one a Dylan Holloway wrist shot with 15 seconds left on a 5% chance, and still fell 5-4 at Grand Casino Arena.

The second period was where the game turned. MIN out-chanced STL 1.47 to 0.51 in expected goals, and Matt Boldy cashed in twice, 27 seconds after Mason McTavish had tied it at 2-2, and again at 16:47 for the 5-2 margin. Kirill Kaprizov tipped one in between. Boldy finished with three goals and a helper on eight shots, and the Wild had 2.84 to 3.12 expected goals on the ice with their top line against about 1.1 allowed. Both goalies finished below expectation, Joel Hofer by 1.33 goals and Jesper Wallstedt by 1.27, so the shot quality, not the goaltending, tells the story.

MIN deserved this one, winning 65% of simulated replays on 3.77 expected goals to 2.73 and 72 shot attempts to 51. The Wild went 1 for 5 on the power play despite 1.64 expected goals with the man advantage, which kept it closer than it should have been. Robert Thomas scored short-handed at 16:00 of the third, and Holloway's goal came with Thomas and Cam Fowler assisting. Fowler had three assists in all, but the comeback arrived one goal too late.
